Every fuel has a §6grade§r, shown in its tooltip. The grade decides which engines can burn it and how well.

- §eLow§r - Heavy Oil, Heating Oil, Industrial Oil, Reclaimed Industrial Oil, the vacuum oils.
- §eMedium§r - Naphtha, Light Oil, Petroil, Coal Gasoline and their cracked, desulfurized and leaded versions.
- §eHigh§r - Diesel, Gasoline, LPG, Reformate, BTX, High-Cetane Diesel, Ethanol, Methanol, Biofuel, NITAN and BF Rocket Fuel.
- §eAviation§r - Kerosene, Jet Fuel and Blood Fuel.
- §eGaseous§r - Natural Gas, Petroleum Gas, Coker Gas, Reformate Gas, Biogas, Syngas and Oxyhydrogen.

§lWho burns what§r
- §3Diesel Generator§r - medium 50%, high 75%, aviation 10%. No low grade.
- §3Radial Performance Engine§r - low 75%, medium 50%, high 25%.
- §3Turbofan§r - aviation only.
- §3Combined Cycle Gas Turbine§r - gaseous only.
- §3Industrial Combustion Engine§r - depends on the piston set: §6Steel§r is best for low grade, §6High-Speed Steel§r for medium, §6Desh§r for high and §6Starmetal§r is good at everything, even gas.
